sections.h2: What is Oglethorpe County like to live in and sell in?
sections.html:
Lexington is the seat of Oglethorpe County, a rural stretch of northeast Georgia that Wikipedia describes as the biggest county in that corner of the state. Lawmakers created it on December 19, 1793, honoring the colony's founder, Gen. James Oglethorpe. Its land came from a tract the Creek and Cherokee gave up to the Colony of Georgia in the treaty of 1773, per Wikipedia.

The county measures 442 square miles, 439 of them land. Most runoff reaches the Broad River on its way to the Savannah, and a thin western strip near Woodville, Crawford and Winterville sends its water to the Upper Oconee. Elbert, Wilkes, Taliaferro, Greene, Oconee, Clarke and Madison counties all touch its edges.

Arnoldsville, Crawford and Lexington are the cities, and Maxeys is a town. Philomath, Point Peter, Sandy Cross, Stephens and Vesta are unincorporated. Visitors come for whitewater rafting on the Broad and South Fork Broad rivers, hunting for deer, turkey and rabbit, an ATV and motorbike park, and antique shopping in historic Lexington, with slices of the Oconee National Forest and Watson Mill Bridge State Park inside the line. Statistically, the county sits in the Athens-Clarke area.

sections.h2: How many people and homes does Oglethorpe County have?
sections.html:
About 16,415 people live across 439 square miles of Oglethorpe County, which works out to just 33.8 per square mile at the 2020 count. Owners live in 83.8% of the homes.

The 2020 census recorded 14,825 residents in 5,803 households, a median age of 43.3 and no urban population at all. Vacancy ran 8.5% of 6,343 housing units, and 19.3% of residents were 65 or older. Getting to work takes 32.8 minutes on average, and 83.6% of households subscribe to broadband. A single district, Oglethorpe County School District, covers every public school address.

sections.h2: What does the Oglethorpe County economy and housing market look like?
sections.html:
Work here is small-scale: QuickFacts counts only 182 employer establishments with 1,104 jobs in 2023, against 1,453 businesses that have no employees. About 60.4% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and 25.3% of adults 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree.

Households average 2.84 people, and 93.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Veterans number 1,138, and 12.2% of residents live in poverty. Builders pulled 80 permits in 2025.

The county's recreation department took the state agency of the year award for populations under 20,000 in 2016, and walkability options are limited across the county.

sections.h2: Who handles Oglethorpe County tax questions?
sections.html:
Walk in at 339 West Main St. in Lexington or write to P.O. Box 305, Lexington, GA 30648. The phone is (706) 743-8422. Hours run 8:00 to 5:00 on weekdays, with a noon to 1:00 closure on Fridays, per the county tax site.

  • Tax Assessors, (706) 743-5166: values, exemptions, appeal paperwork
  • Board of Equalization: Grand Jury appointees who rule on challenges to assessor values
  • County commissioners and school board: each adopts its own mill rate
  • Deed room, Oglethorpe County Courthouse: copies of warranty deeds

The same office registers motor vehicles as the state's agent. It has no say over value or millage, so a complaint about either belongs with the assessors or the boards that set rates.

sections.h2: When is Oglethorpe County tax due, and what do late payers owe?
sections.html:
December 20 is the normal deadline for real estate and business personal property tax, according to the county's tax FAQ. Mobile and manufactured homes are due April 1, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday.

  • Interest of 1% a month builds from December 21 onward
  • A 10% penalty hits tax still open after 90 days, with homesteaded property owing less than $500 excused
  • Beyond 90 days, a FiFa lien can go on record at the Clerk of Superior Court
  • A mobile home past April 1 picks up a 10% filing penalty and 1% monthly, and may end up at auction

Bills are addressed to the homeowner, not the lender, so an owner with an escrow account must pass the bill to the servicer. The FAQ adds that recorded liens are open records that credit bureaus may use.

sections.h2: Does Oglethorpe County really assess city property at 100%?
sections.html:
That is what the county tax FAQ states: 40% of fair market value at the county level and 100% at the city level. Before assuming a number, ask the tax office or the city clerk which base and which levies cover your parcel.

The tax site walks through the arithmetic: market value as of January 1, then 40% of it, then exemptions off the top, then millage on what remains.

The state revenue commissioner reviews county digests so assessments stay even between counties, and the state's own ad valorem levy cannot exceed one quarter of a mill.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a value or claim homestead in Oglethorpe County?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors inside 45 days of the notice date and say which method you prefer. The reasons it can rest on are taxability, value, uniformity and a refused exemption.

Mobile homes have their own timing: 45 days from the mailing of the bill to declare another value, then 21 days from the notice to carry a dispute to the Board of Equalization. The assessors answer at (706) 743-5166.

  • You qualify by owning the house and living in it on January 1
  • The application can arrive in any month, but one received after April 1 takes effect the following year
  • Remain in the same house and the exemption carries on without a new form
  • A move means a new application for the new address
  • At age 62 an owner may apply for an additional exemption

sections.h2: What should an Oglethorpe County seller check before closing?
sections.html:
Get a payoff in writing from the Tax Commissioner and search for liens at the Clerk of Superior Court. A FiFa can follow tax left open past 90 days, so check the docket early.

The deed room at the Oglethorpe County Courthouse can copy your warranty deed. For a mobile home, the decal comes with payment of the year's tax and must be displayed, and the location permit depends on that tax being paid in full.

If you buy another house, file a new homestead application there. Questions on balances or decals go to (706) 743-8422.

faqs.a: The county covers 442 square miles, of which 439 are land. That works out to 33.8 residents per square mile at the 2020 count, and Wikipedia calls it the largest county in Northeast Georgia.

faqs.q: Which river carries most of the water out of Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: The Broad River. Most of the county sits in the Broad River sub-basin of the Savannah River basin, with a narrow western strip draining to the Upper Oconee and a small southern part to the Little River.

faqs.q: When was Oglethorpe County founded, and for whom is it named?
faqs.a: It was founded on December 19, 1793 and is named for Georgia's founder, Gen. James Oglethorpe. The land was part of a tract the Creek and Cherokee surrendered to the Colony of Georgia in 1773.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for late tax in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: A 10% penalty applies 90 days after the December 20 deadline, plus 1% interest a month from the due date. Homesteaded property owing under $500 escapes the penalty.

faqs.q: Where can I get a copy of my deed in Oglethorpe County?
faqs.a: At the deed room of the Clerk of Superior Court, inside the Oglethorpe County Courthouse in Lexington.
